wins.text: Firm reported net income of $16.5B and EPS of $5.94 with ROTC of 23%; revenue up 10% YoY to $15.5B driven by higher markets revenue, IB fees, and NII
CIB reported net income of $9B on revenue of $23.4B, up 19% YoY; IB fees up 28% YoY on strong M&A and equity underwriting; Fixed income markets up 21% YoY; Equities up 17% YoY
AWM AUM of $4.8T up 16% YoY; client assets of $7.1T up 18% YoY; long-term net inflows of $54B with strength across fixed income, equity and multi-asset; pretax margin of 35%
CCB home lending originations of $13.7B increased 46% YoY driven by refi performance; client investment assets up 18% YoY; average deposits up 2% YoY and QoQ

Consumer and small business spending remains resilient with spend growth above last year's pace; no signs of cracks in credit metrics — early roll rates, delinquency rates, cash buffers all consistent with prior healthy trends

risks.text: Basel III endgame and G-SIB reproposal would require JPM's CET1 capital to increase ~4% (vs. Fed estimate of ~5% reduction for large banks broadly); G-SIB surcharge rising to 5.2% in 2028 from 4.5%, adding ~$20B of incremental capital requirements based on current balance sheet
Expenses of $26.9B were up 14% YoY, outpacing revenue growth of 10%; Q1 annualized run rate implies potential upward pressure on the $105B full-year expense guide if markets remain strong
Total NII guidance revised down: markets NII now expected at ~$8B (reduced from prior estimate), predominantly due to lower rates; partially offset in NIR but represents a net headwind
Geopolitical developments in the Middle East flagged as a risk to IB deal execution and timing; higher energy prices could eventually fracture consumer resilience if labor market weakens

Net reserve build of $191M and net charge-offs of $2.3B; management debated adding downside scenario weighting given macro uncertainty but held off — leaving potential for larger reserve builds if conditions deteriorate

guidance_items.detail: NII ex-markets continues to be expected at ~$95B for full year 2026
Total NII now expected at ~$103B; markets NII revised down to ~$8B from prior estimate, predominantly due to lower rates, expected to be primarily offset in NIR
Adjusted expense outlook continues to be ~$105B for full year 2026
Card net charge-off rate continues to be approximately 3.4%

Stablecoin/digital assets regulatory landscape and implications for JPM's payments franchise
LLM-enabled cybersecurity risks and systemic preparedness of the banking system
